subject: Urgent: Reserved GPU capacity ceiling impacting production - request for ops deck and exec touch
messages:
From: Samantha Todd <samantha.todd@acmehealth.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.com>, Monica Patel <monica.patel@redwood.com>
Cc: sales_ops@acmehealth.com
Date: Wed, 01 Sep 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Production latency + errors — reserved capacity shortfall (urgent)

Marcus / Monica,

We started seeing sustained latency > 600ms and 503 error spikes on our critical inference route (patient-notes-summarize) around 08:50 PT this morning. This is on our reserved capacity plan — we were expecting steady throughput for peak business hours. The attached snippet (acme_error_sample.log) shows token-level timeouts and KV-cache misses.

Impact: ~18% of requests have 5xx or timeouts over the past 20 minutes; our SLA is 99.9% at p95 and we’re already outside the acceptable window. This is causing downstream retries in our pipeline and elevated customer complaints.

Immediate ask: can Redwood confirm whether our dedicated pool is saturated or if there’s a routing/regression on your side? We need an operational update and a plan for the next 2 hours — including any temporary mitigation you can apply (burst capacity, model fallback, or routing changes).

I’m available now for a quick sync; please include SRE/ops and someone who can authorize temporary burst/credits if needed.

Thanks,
Samantha Todd
Head of ML Platforms
Acme Health

Attachments: acme_error_sample.log (text, 47 KB)

Samantha — thanks for the alert and the log sample. We’re treating this as a priority.

Immediate steps (short bullets):
- Monica/Aditya: can you confirm pool utilization and active queue depths for Acme's reserved slice? Share real-time metrics to the Drive link and Slack #escalations.
- Samantha: we’ll propose a short mitigation plan (burst allocation + routing to a lower-quantized model variant) and ask your permission to enable it for a 2-hour window.
- I’ll schedule a 30-min bridge in 15 minutes for triage and exec sync if required.

We will escalate internally to secure any necessary temporary headroom from dedicated capacity. I’ll loop in Marissa on exec attention if the issue persists after mitigations.

—Marcus

Subject: Re: Production latency + errors — reserved capacity shortfall (urgent)

Thanks Samantha — I pulled the telemetry and here's what I see so far:

Summary (quick):
- Reserved GPU slice for Acme is at 92% GPU compute utilization and active request queue depth has spiked 4x vs baseline.
- Latency correlates with large-batched replays that began at 08:45 PT from a downstream analytics job (batch-window ingestion). Those batches are monopolizing KV-cache slots and causing LRU thrash.
- No infra regression detected in the last 24 hours (kernel/kernel-driver versions unchanged). There is, however, an increased proportion of long-context requests (avg seq_len > 2048) which increases per-token compute.

Proposed mitigations (we can enact immediately with your sign-off):
1) Route 20% of traffic to the same model family in 4-bit quantized variant (maintains output quality for this route historically) — reduces per-token GPU time ~35%.
2) Apply short-lived 2-hour burst from shared Dedicated pool (we can push 30% extra headroom for Acme if approved).
3) Temporarily pause non-critical large-batch replay jobs in your environment (we can coordinate the exact job ids) — this would free KV-cache resources and smooth latency in 20-30 minutes.
4) Enable prefix caching on your most common prompt templates (we'll pre-warm cache for the top 3 templates).

I attached a one-page mitigation plan and checklist (mitigation-plan.pdf) with owner assignments and rollback steps. If we get go-ahead for #1 and #2 now I can flip the routing policy and request the burst within 10 minutes.

Next steps: Marcus — recommend we run the 15-min bridge now and get a short exec note ready for Acme if they request it. Samantha — please confirm you want us to proceed with the routing change and burst.

—Monica
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Attachments: mitigation-plan.pdf (PDF, 120 KB)
